newsitem.title: EGYPT: Libya says stranded Palestinians to go home Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Libya says stranded Palestinians to go home Tuesday.

text.p: Libya said on Sunday that Palestinians stranded in appalling conditions on the Libyan-Egyptian border for more than a year could return to Libya on Tuesday.

But humanitarian organisations said that many of the 200 to 250 refugees did not want to go to Libya and it was unclear what would be available for them if they did go back. The Palestinians had been in Libya as workers, students or their respective families.

Eric Stobbarts, the head of the Medecins sans Frontieres (MSF) office in Egypt, told Reuters: "There is a lot of reluctance among the refugees about returning without guarantees of a normal life. There is no guarantee of jobs or anything."

MSF, an international medical charity, is the only organisation with staff permanently based in the camp, which lies in no-man's land between the Egyptian and Libyan border posts near Salloum on the Mediterranean coast.
"The majority are reluctant to return... Some of them have no links with Libya, like one person from Mali, one from Senegal and some Palestinians expelled from Egypt," Stobbarts said.
Panos Moumtzis, the representative in Egypt of the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR, said that he found mixed reaction in the camp.
"Some welcomed it, but there are more than 20 Palestinians who have Egyptian wives and want to be reunited with them in Egypt," he said. "Others have just been dumped there," he added.
Many of the Palestinians have been stuck in the camp since Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi expelled them in September 1995 in an attempt to show the futility of the PLO-Israeli peace deal.
Libya reversed the policy last Tuesday, saying it was not possible for the Palestinians to go home to Palestine. It has not said what will happen to those who do not want to go back.
Most of the Palestinians expelled from Libya went to countries beyond Egypt but Egypt refused to admit those who had no proof they could continue to another country.
They cannot go to the Palestinian territories because Israel continues to control immigration there.
